To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the combination of laser scanners and camera systems is a powerful sensor system for the task of building a geometrical model of an unknown environment and for navigation purposes; 2) the sensor fusion of such a combination of sensors is possible and leads to an increased performance of the system; and 3) the use of a common representation for all sensor data and the use of a Kalman filter for the sensor fusion is a powerful tool.

A mobile service robot that uses sensor-fusion techniques for the integration of complementary sensor information, like laser scanners and cameras, is able to build a model of its environment and navigate through it."
A mobile service robot can explore an unknown environment by using a combination of a 2D-laser scanner and a camera.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mobile service robots that are capable to operate in dynamic environments and interact with human beings and static and moving objects.
the development of an integrated system of a mobile service- robot and a sensor system.
sensor integration and sensor fusion of complementary sensors for mobile service robots in dynamic and changing environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sensor integration and sensor-fusion techniques are very useful for mobile service-robot applications, especially when the robot is operating in a dynamic and changing environments.
the presented sensor integration and fusion techniques are a valuable contribution for mobile robots in a dynamic and changing environment, like a hospital.
the sensor fusion techniques described are suitable to achieve the goal of a mobile service robot operating in a natural environment together with humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sensor fusion is an important step in the development of mobile service-robot systems that operate in natural environments.
sensor-fusion of the laser scanner with a camera system is possible, but the results are still not satisfying.
the described approach for integrating and fusing the sensor data is a promising approach to achieve the desired robustness of the mobile service-robots in a dynamic and changing environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a sensor fusion system can be built by combining a number of different sensor modalities, which are not necessarily calibrated.
sensor fusion is a powerful and robust technique to integrate complementary sensors and that it can be applied successfully to a mobile service robot.
